The '''2018–19 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kentucky]] in the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The team played its home games in [[Lexington, Kentucky]] for the 43rd consecutive season at [[Rupp Arena]], with a capacity of 20,500. The Wildcats, led by [[John Calipari]] in his 10th season as head coach, played in the [[Southeastern Conference]].

==Previous season==
The [[2017–18 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Wildcats]] finished the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]] 26–11, 10–8 in [[2017–18 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|SEC play]] to finish in a three-way tie for fourth. In the [[2018 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], the Wildcats defeated [[2017–18 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|Georgia]], [[2017–18 Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball team|Alabama]], and [[2017–18 Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball team|Tennessee]] to win the tournament championship for the 31st time in school history. As a result, the Wildcats received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As the No. 5 seed in the South region, they defeated No. 12 [[2017–18 Davidson Wildcats men's basketball team|Davidson]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/kentucky/2018/03/15/kentucky-basketball-march-madness-davidson-uk-wildcats-ncaa-tournament/421001002/|title=Kentucky basketball moves past Davidson into NCAA Tournament second round|work=courier-journal.com|access-date=2018-03-26|language=en-US}}</ref> and No. 13 [[2017–18 Buffalo Bulls men's basketball team|Buffalo]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/game?gameId=401025858|title=Buffalo vs. Kentucky - Game Recap - March 17, 2018 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-03-26}}</ref> There, they lost to No. 9-seeded [[2017–18 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401025877|title=Kansas St vs. Kentucky - Game Recap - March 22, 2018 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-06-28}}</ref>

===2018 recruiting class===
[[Immanuel Quickley]], from [[Havre de Grace, Maryland]], was the first commitment to Kentucky's 2018 class. He committed to Kentucky on September 22, over offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]]. He was a consensus five-star prospect and was ranked the consensus No. 12 overall player by the four main recruiting services. The Wildcats' second 2018 commitment was [[Keldon Johnson]], a small forward from [[South Hill, Virginia]], who committed on November 11. Kentucky beat out [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]], [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]], and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] for Johnson's signature. He was also a consensus five-star prospect and was ranked by ESPN as its No. 7 overall prospect.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/21380165/keldon-johnson-no-7-recruit-espn-100-commits-kentucky-wildcats |title=Keldon Johnson, No. 7 recruit in ESPN 100, joins Kentucky's 2018 class |first=Jeff |last=Borzello |publisher=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 11, 2017 |access-date=November 12, 2017}}</ref> Tyler Herro was the third commitment for Kentucky's 2018 class. Formerly committed to [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]], he committed to Kentucky the week after his official visit. Herro was a consensus four-star prospect and was ranked the No. 4 shooting guard in the 2018 class by ESPN. E.J. Montgomery was the fourth commitment for Kentucky's 2018 class. Formerly committed to [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], he re-opened his recruitment after the Auburn staff was implicated in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball corruption scandal]]. Montgomery committed to Kentucky on April 9, 2018. He was a five-star prospect and was ranked No. 12 in the 2018 class.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23088894/ej-montgomery-latest-5-star-recruit-commit-kentucky-wildcats |title=E.J. Montgomery latest 5-star recruit to commit to Kentucky|first=Jeff |last=Borzello |publisher=[[ESPN.com]] |date=April 9, 2018 |access-date=April 9, 2018}}</ref> On April 10, 2018, Ashton Hagans committed to the University of Kentucky over offers from [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|Georgia]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]. Hagans was originally the second commitment in the 2019 recruiting class and the No. 1 ranked point guard in the class of 2019 by 247 sports. On June 15, 2018, Hagans announced that he would be [[reclassification (education)|reclassifying]] into the 2018 class and would play for the Cats in the upcoming season, thus making him the fifth recruit in the class of 2018.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://kentuckysportsradio.com/basketball-2/ashton-hagans-graduates-will-officially-reclassify-to-class-of-2018/ |title=Ashton Hagans graduates, will officially reclassify to class of 2018|first=Jack |last=Pilgram |publisher=KentuckySportsRadio.com |date=June 15, 2018 |access-date=June 15, 2018}}</ref>{{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2018}}

===Incoming transfers===
On June 20, 2018, Reid Travis announced that he would transfer to Kentucky.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/06/20/reid-travis-grad-transfer-kentucky-wildcats-next-season-outlook|title=What Reid Travis transferring to Kentucky means|work=SI.com|access-date=2018-06-28|language=en}}</ref> He was a two-time first team All-Pac-12 for [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] and averaged 19.5 PPG and 8.7 RPG in his final year with the Cardinal. As a grad transfer, he was eligible to play immediately.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23852982/reid-travis-announces-transfer-stanford-kentucky|title=Stanford's Travis transferring to Kentucky|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-06-28}}</ref>
